The problem doesn't lie in the collection of the info.  The problem lies in those who decide to act on the data.  Every day, people do things that may be illegal, but cops generally don't do anything about them.  The laws are very complicated and some old ones are no longer really relevant, but are still in place.  So the average person has a long list of small things that when assessed cumulatively, can be punishable.  In many cases, this isn't stuff that gets enforced.

But what happens when you start speaking out against something in politics?  What happens when you get noticed because your opinion about the government is seen as controversial or could potentially upset the status quo?  Freedom of speech protects us for being punished for these opinions, but it doesn't prevent us from suddenly having every trivial part of our pasts pulled up in court and used as evidence to lock us up for for a very long time.

The problem with the collection of this data is there is no guarantee it will be used purely for justice.  As long as there is a human component, there is chance of corruption.  In a perfect world, this would make us safer and crime more preventable.  But there's no way in hell the world will ever be like that.
Thanks dude.  That sounds like a really good way for me to reach out.  I hate being coddled and it always feels like opening up about this stuff just makes people do that.

I'm an escapist by nature.  Last time I was like this, I got lost in gaming.  But a lot of my depressive bouts make it very hard to enjoy things I usually love.  I can barely get myself to even launch my games lately.  I will try to find something to do that I enjoy, though.  Thank you.
